reasoning: The edge type DEPENDS_ON is wrong. The note itself admits this is a which-came-first argument ("which-came-first: writing predates science"), which is the test for DERIVED_FROM, not DEPENDS_ON. Under Law 8a, if your reasoning is by chronology, the edge must be DERIVED_FROM. Furthermore, under Law 8, DEPENDS_ON requires present-tense necessity: if you remove writing right now, does science stop working? No — science as a method of inquiry (observation, experimentation, reasoning) functions perfectly without writing. Writing is a tool for recording science, not a constitutive requirement. The correct edge would be DERIVED_FROM (science derives from the historical development of writing as a recording tool), or possibly no edge at all if the relationship is merely facilitative.

Under Law 8, DEPENDS_ON requires present-tense necessity: does compilation stop working if you remove algorithms? No — algorithms are what compilation implements, not a prerequisite. This is an INSTANCE_OF relationship (compilation is a kind of algorithmic process) or possibly DERIVED_FROM (compilation derives from the historical development of algorithms). The note also uses "which-came-first" language, which is the DERIVED_FROM test per Law 8a. A compiler does not depend on algorithms any more than a car depends on the concept of motion.
